source_span: Despite the sequential pickup in August, we estimate that core PCE inflation has slowed to a 2.5% annualized pace over the last three months... This slowdown mostly reflects the waning impulses from tariff pass-through, energy pass-through, and software/accessories price hikes.
source_chain: August core PCE ticked up 0.27% MoM therefore the Fed turned hawkish for one more hike (Oct 27-28), but temporary pass-through effects (tariff/energy/software) are already fading therefore the 3-month-annualized core PCE rate has slowed to 2.5% therefore Goldman expects only that one hike then a flat rate with cuts from late 2027; invalidation is a fresh, non-fading inflation shock, not the August print itself.
pulse_chain: Goldman's one-hike-then-flat call rests on core PCE running 2.5% annualized therefore that case needs the data to cooperate, but August's 0.27% print (plus a Saudi-strike oil jump) instead breaks it therefore the short-cycle case has no answer for the energy shock; invalidation is the 10-year closing decisively above 5% versus BTIG's 4.92% flip level.
why: The pulse turns Goldman's own cited August core-PCE print (0.27% MoM) into evidence that Goldman's disinflation call is failing, but Goldman's note already folds that exact print into its 2.5% three-month-annualized figure and concludes deceleration is intact and temporary effects are fading, so the pulse reverses the note's conclusion about its own headline number instead of reproducing it.
